correctness.rationale: Let \(A=\operatorname{aff}C=a+L\). At every \(y\in\operatorname{ri}C\), the convex normal cone is exactly \(L^\perp\). If \(C\) is non-affine and \(\bar y\in\operatorname{relbd}C\), relative separation supplies a unit supporting normal \(u\in L\cap N_C(\bar y)\). Along any relative-interior sequence \(y_k\to\bar y\), the point \(ru\in N_C(\bar y)\cap B_r\) has Euclidean distance exactly \(r\) from \(L^\perp\cap B_r=N_C(y_k)\cap B_r\). Thus the Hausdorff distance is at least \(r\) while the base points coalesce, proving discontinuity. Conversely, if \(C=a+L\), every normal cone is \(L^\perp\), so the truncated map is constant. The source's form (3) is exactly this fixed-radius truncation, so the application follows without changing definitions.

value.rationale: The result is a natural complete classification of a recent algorithmic regularity assumption, not an arbitrary slice. The primary paper explicitly permits general closed constraints and highlights the easy strongly convex projection step when the constraint set is convex, so determining exactly which convex sets satisfy its normal-map hypothesis materially changes the usable scope of the convergence guarantee. The fixed jump \(r\) shows the obstruction is structural rather than a poor Lipschitz constant: every genuine convex boundary fails continuity itself. This cleanly separates the source's general-set truncation from its manifold construction and identifies what a future analysis would need to weaken if it is to cover boxes, balls, polyhedra, and other standard convex constraint sets.
